event_name: Constantine I dedicates Constantinople as capital
description: The Roman Emperor Constantine the Great dedicates the city on the site of ancient Byzantium as the new imperial capital.
Crusader knights capture and sack the city; the Byzantine population and economy do not recover to prior scale before 1453 (see population_context.csv).
Control passes back to the Greeks under the Palaiologan dynasty after the Latin interregnum.
Bayezid I builds a fortress on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus, the future counterpart to Rumelihisari.
Sultan whose conquest and rebuilding programme frame this entire project (see campaign_timeline.csv and post_conquest_transformation.csv for detail).

event_name: Fall of Constantinople / conquest of the city
description: 29 May 1453; end of the Byzantine Empire and start of the city's transformation into the Ottoman capital. See campaign_timeline.csv for a day-level account.

event_name: Founding infrastructure of the Ottoman capital
description: Topkapi Palace, the Fatih Mosque complex, and the formal relocation of the capital from Edirne, all under Mehmed II. See post_conquest_transformation.csv.
Household census records 16,324 households on the Istanbul side. See population_1477_households.csv.

event_name: Population growth and disputed scale under later 16th-century sultans
description: Historians cited by Oz give widely varying estimates (roughly 400,000-700,000) for the city's 16th-century population; no single figure is treated as settled in the sources reviewed.
The 1509 earthquake ('Lesser Judgment Day' in later tradition) damages Rumelihisari, which is subsequently repaired.

Major architectural addition to the Ottoman capital's skyline under Suleyman I, illustrating continued imperial investment in the city (general architectural-history knowledge; not independently sourced in this project's search results).

event_name: Ottoman printing press established in Istanbul
description: Ibrahim Muteferrika's press marks an early institutional step in the city's print culture (general historical knowledge; not independently sourced in this project's search results).
Administrative and legal modernization reforms centered on Istanbul as the imperial capital (general historical knowledge; not independently sourced in this project's search results).

event_name: First official Ottoman census of the city
description: First modern census records roughly 875,000 residents. See population_context.csv (P10).

event_name: Ankara becomes capital of the Turkish Republic
description: Istanbul loses its political-capital status after roughly 1,600 years (330-1453 as Byzantine/Roman capital, 1453-1922 as Ottoman capital) though it remains the country's largest city and commercial-cultural center (general historical knowledge; not independently sourced in this project's search results).

event_name: First Turkish Republic census of the city
description: 691,000 residents within municipal boundaries, down from roughly 1,200,000 in the World War I era. See population_context.csv (P11).
Province population grows from roughly 1.17 million (1950) to just over 10 million (2000) across successive national censuses. See population_context.csv (P12-P15).

event_name: Historic Areas of Istanbul inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
description: Inscription (ref. 356) covers several zones including the Theodosian land walls.

event_name: Continued growth to roughly 15.0-15.8 million residents
description: Address-Based Population Registration System figures place the province at approximately 15.0 million (2017), 15.8 million (2021), approximately 15.7 million (2023) and 15,754,053 (end of 2025). See population_context.csv (P16-P19).
